script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: "The Late Bloomer"

INT. FRANK'S APARTMENT - DAY

*A cramped, cluttered living room with books stacked to the ceiling and papers strewn about. Frank, a disheveled, middle-aged man, sits on the couch with a laptop.*

FRANK: (muttering to himself) Come on, just one more revision...

Suddenly, a loud knock at the door.

FRANK: (surprised) Who could that be?

*He gets up from the couch and opens the door to reveal EMMA, a bright, cheery woman in her late 20s, holding a bouquet of flowers.*

EMMA: (smiling) Hi, Frank! I'm your new neighbor. I thought I'd bring you a welcome gift.

FRANK: (stunned) Oh, uh, hello. Please come in.

*Emma enters the apartment, her eyes widening at the clutter. Frank leads her into the living room.*

EMMA: Wow, you're quite the collector, Frank.

FRANK: (sheepishly) I... um, write. A lot.

EMMA: (laughs) Well, it's a lovely mess. I'm Emma, by the way.

FRANK: (smiling) Nice to meet you, Emma.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

*A few days later, Frank and Emma sit at a table, sipping coffees.*

FRANK: So, Emma, what do you do?

EMMA: I'm a graphic designer. I work for a marketing firm downtown.

FRANK: That's impressive. I've been trying to write a novel for years, but I just can't seem to get it right.

EMMA: (smiling) Well, maybe I can help you out. I've always wanted to write a book, too. We could be writing partners.

FRANK: (surprised) Really? That would be amazing.

INT. FRANK'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

*Frank and Emma sit at Frank's kitchen table, surrounded by papers and laptops. They brainstorm ideas for Frank's novel.*

EMMA: How about a story about second chances? You know, where the protagonist gets a do-over in life?

FRANK: (excited) That's a great idea! What if the protagonist is an older guy who's never really lived life to the fullest?

EMMA: Ooh, I like that. And what if he gets a chance to go back in time and relive his youth, but this time, he makes different choices?

FRANK: (grinning) I think we've got something here.

INT. EMMA'S APARTMENT - DAY

*A few weeks later, Frank and Emma sit on Emma's couch, laughing as they read through the first draft of Frank's novel.*

EMMA: (teasingly) You know, you're a pretty good writer, Frank.

FRANK: (blushing) I couldn't have done it without you, Emma.

EMMA: (smiling) Well, we make a good team.

INT. PARK - DAY

*Frank and Emma sit on a blanket in the park, surrounded by cherry blossom trees in full bloom. They read from Frank's manuscript, each taking turns reading aloud.*

FRANK: (reading) "And then, she looked at him with those bright, sparkling eyes, and he knew that he was truly alive for the first time in his life."

EMMA: (laughing) That's a beautiful line, Frank.

FRANK: (grinning) I couldn't have written it without your help.

EMMA: (smiling) I'm just glad I could be a part of it.

INT. FRANK'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

*Frank sits at his desk, staring at the finished manuscript. He looks up as he hears a knock at the door.*

FRANK: (surprised) Who could that be?

*He opens the door to reveal an older version of himself, wearing a suit and carrying a briefcase. Older Frank looks exhausted and worn out.*

OLDER FRANK: (wearily) Hi, Frank. I'm you, from the future.

FRANK: (shocked) What? How is that possible?

OLDER FRANK: (sighing) Long story. The point is, I came back to tell you that your novel is going to change lives. People are going to read it and be inspired to take second chances in their own lives.

FRANK: (astonished) Really?

OLDER FRANK: (nodding) Yes. And I wanted to thank you, Frank. For letting me be a part of it.

FRANK: (smiling) I'm just glad I could help, even if it was just a small part.

OLDER FRANK: (smiling back) Trust me, it's not a small part.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

*A few months later, Frank and Emma sit at their usual table, sipping coffees and laughing as they brainstorm ideas for Frank's next novel.*

EMMA: (laughing) You know, Frank, I think we've got a real knack for this.

FRANK: (grinning) I couldn't agree more. And who knows? Maybe one day, our novels will be turned into movies.

EMMA: (giggling) I'd love that.

FRANK: (looking thoughtful) Or even better, maybe we could write a screenplay together.

EMMA: (excited) That's a great idea, Frank! Let's do it.

INT. STUDIO - DAY

*A year later, Frank and Emma sit in a studio, watching as actors read from their screenplay. They smile and nod as the actors bring their characters to life.*

EMMA: (whispering to Frank) I can't believe it, Frank. Our screenplay is actually being made into a movie.

FRANK: (grinning) I know, it's surreal. But I'm just glad we got this chance to live out our dreams.

EMMA: (smiling) Me too, Frank. Me too.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
